content: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has proposed subsidising liability insurance for state and local police officers who enforce federal immigration laws, in an aim to shield officers who are accused of on-duty misconduct. The Associated Press first reported the news, citing an ICE planning document detailing the policy. According to the planning document, police officers would purchase liability insurance covering up to $500,000 – which could cover legal fees and settlements – for about $250 per year, and then be reimbursed that amount by ICE. A northern California county that has become a hotbed of activism for those who sow doubts about the reliability of voting machines plans to hire Tina Peters, the prominent Colorado election denier recently released from prison, to work on elections. Clint Curtis, the top election official in Shasta county, told the Guardian he plans to hire Peters as a consultant to replace Brent Turner, his top deputy, who has been on medical leave. He said Peters would not have access to the county’s voting system. Plans to hire Peters were first reported by Action News Now. Shasta county, a conservative region home to 182,000 people, has emerged as a center of the US election denialism movement in recent years. In 2023, the county’s governing body unsuccessfully sought to remake the voting process by cutting ties with the voting machine company Dominion Voting Systems and implementing a hand-count system that experts warned would be costly and far less accurate. The MyPillow CEO Mike Lindell, one of the leading promoters of falsehoods about election fraud in the US, said he would support the county’s effort. The state ultimately blocked Shasta’s plans. In addition, several candidates who lost their race for local office have embraced baseless conspiracy theories about election fraud and sued to overturn results. Read our full report below: Donald Trump voted by mail in Florida’s Republican primary, Politico reports, citing Palm Beach County voting records. In March, the president signed an executive ⁠order restricting the use of mail-in ballots ahead of the November midterm elections that will decide control of US Congress. Trump has repeatedly criticized mail-in voting, calling for restrictions on the policy for years and falsely claiming that his 2020 election defeat was the result of widespread voter fraud. A federal judge has blocked ⁠the US Postal ⁠Service from implementing part of the executive order, although Trump’s administration has asked the supreme court to intervene. “What a joke. It’s almost like Donald Trump thinks we’re a bunch of idiots. The President whines about mail-in voting day after day, only to turn around and vote by mail himself. If he can lie so comfortably about the integrity of mail-in voting, just imagine what else he’s lying to all of us about,” said Jonah Bryson of Voters of Tomorrow, a political action committee focused on Gen-Z voters. A federal judge halted the Trump administration’s effort to relocate the FBI headquarters to Washington DC, rather than a congressionally approved site in Maryland. US District Judge Theodore Chuang sided with Marlyand’s attorney general and Prince George’s County, where the new FBI headquarters is slated to be located. Chuang wrote that the Trump administration’s selection of the Ronald Reagan Building in Washington violated congressional measures requiring the General Services Administration to select one of three locations outside Washington. “Maryland and Prince George’s County committed more than a decade of work to earn the FBI headquarters and pledged hundreds of millions of dollars. By blocking the Trump Administration’s unlawful attempt to move the FBI to the Reagan Building and divert the funds Congress set aside for this project, the Court has cleared the path back to Greenbelt,” Maryland attorney general Anthony G. Brown said in a statement. Turkish president Recep Tayyip Erdoğan urged Donald Trump ⁠in a ⁠call today to continue talks with Iran to de-escalate ⁠tensions between the two countries, and offered Ankara’s ⁠support in peace efforts, the ‌Turkish presidency ‌said. In a ‌statement, the presidency said Erdoğan and Trump also discussed Israel’s war in Gaza, a defence ‌pact signed between Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan, and bilateral ties. It added that Erdogan told Trump that Israel’s attacks ⁠on Palestinians in Gaza had increased at a time when the second phase ‌of Trump’s peace plan was supposed to come into effect. Donald Trump again threatened to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of his effort to end the US-Israel war on Iran, as the two-month window to negotiate peace with Iran expired on Monday with no end to the conflict in sight. “If Oman gets in the way, we’ll bomb the shit out of them,” Trump told Fox News, the second time he has directed such a threat at Muscat, a longtime US strategic partner that has traditionally served as a key backchannel between Washington and Tehran. Trump ⁠said that North Korean leader ⁠Kim Jong-un ⁠had responded ‌to his overtures ‌after he ‌ordered the US to scale back military ‌exercises with South Korea. Speaking ‌to reporters in the Oval ‌Office, Trump was asked why Kim had not responded to his overtures. Trump shot back at the reporter: “How do you know he hasn’t responded?” The reporter then asked again if he had. “Um, yeah he has,” Trump said. Asked what stage the conversations with Kim were at, Trump said “it’s very positive”, but provided no further detail. Trump also claimed he had third-hand reports that the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln is “beautifully maintained” despite extensive accounts of deteriorating living conditions during its lengthy deployment in the strait of Hormuz. “The Lincoln has been out there for a period of time – a good period of time – but over the years, we’ve had them out there much longer,” Trump said, describing an exchange with a veteran, whom he did not name, over the weekend. chineseContent: 移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 提议为执行联邦移民法的州和地方警察提供责任保险补贴，以保护被指控有不当行为的警察。美联社首先报道了这一消息，并援引了 ICE 详细介绍该政策的规划文件。根据规划文件，警察将每年购买约 250 美元的责任保险，保额高达 50 万美元，可用于支付法律费用和和解费用，然后由 ICE 报销该金额。加州北部的一个县已成为那些对投票机可靠性产生怀疑的人激进主义的温床，该县计划聘请最近出狱的科罗拉多州著名选举否认者蒂娜·彼得斯 (Tina Peters) 从事选举工作。沙斯塔县最高选举官员克林特·柯蒂斯告诉《卫报》，他计划聘请彼得斯作为顾问，以取代一直休病假的最高副手布伦特·特纳。他说彼得斯将无法进入该县的投票系统。 Action News Now 最先报道了雇用彼得斯的计划。沙斯塔县是一个拥有 182,000 人的保守地区，近年来已成为美国否认选举运动的中心。 2023 年，该县管理机构试图通过切断与投票机公司 Dominion Voting Systems 的联系并实施手工计票系统来重新制定投票流程，但没有成功，专家警告称，该系统成本高昂且准确性低得多。 MyPillow 首席执行官迈克·林德尔 (Mike Lindell) 是美国选举舞弊谎言的主要推动者之一，他表示将支持该县的努力。该州最终阻止了沙斯塔的计划。此外，几位在地方公职竞选中落败的候选人也接受了
